card.occupation: Care assistant at a privately run residential care home for older people, about 24 hours a week over three long day shifts
card.education_detail: Left a local comprehensive at 16 with a handful of GCSEs (C in English, D in maths). Did a few years of shop and bar work, then an NVQ Level 2 in Health and Social Care through her first care job. She is part-way through a Level 3 diploma her employer pays for, and is behind on the written units.
card.household: Rents a three-bed ex-council semi with her partner of nine years, Dean (44, forklift driver at a distribution warehouse off the M1), and her son Kai (16, from a previous relationship, doing his GCSEs). They have never married. She says they will 'when someone else pays for it'. There is also a French bulldog called Tyson, which she bought on finance.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Ashfield. Her mum still lives two streets away, and her grandad was a miner at one of the local pits before the closures. She was christened Church of England and has her nan's gold cross, which she wears most days. She goes to church at Christmas, Remembrance Sunday and funerals, and calls herself Christian without thinking much more about it. Her family is close, loud and full of feuds. Sunday dinner at her mum's is a fixture.
card.professional_persona: Popular with residents and families because she is warm, funny and remembers everyone's grandchildren's names, and she enjoys being the one families ask for. Less popular with some colleagues. She is good at disappearing when there is a hoist job going, she has been known to round her timesheet up, and she makes sure managers hear about the things she does well. She gets genuinely upset when a resident she's fond of dies, and she worries a lot about being blamed if something goes wrong on shift.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She did a Couch to 5K app twice and stopped at week four both times. She walks Tyson round the reservoir and counts her steps on a smartwatch, which she will tell you about. She watches the darts and Love Island with equal commitment and goes to the odd Mansfield Town game with Dean, mostly for the bar.
card.arts_persona: Loves a big night out at a show: Mamma Mia in Nottingham, a tribute act at the local club, a comedian at the Motorpoint Arena. She reads the odd thriller on holiday, watches a lot of true crime documentaries, and has strong opinions about reality TV.
card.travel_persona: One week abroad a year if they can manage it, usually all-inclusive in Tenerife or Turkey, booked on a deposit and paid off monthly. She enjoys the photos as much as the holiday and posts plenty. They do weekends in Skegness with the caravan crowd from her mum's side. She'd love Dubai 'just to say I've been'.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks quick family food in the week: pasta bakes, air fryer chicken, a 'fakeaway' on Fridays. Her mum does the proper roast on Sundays. She calls the midday meal dinner and the evening meal tea, and a bread roll is a cob. Likes a pink gin, a Chinese takeaway on payday, and anything she's seen on TikTok that week.
hobbies_and_interests: Getting her nails done every three weeks and following nail artists on Instagram
Selling clothes and bits on Vinted, and buying 'designer' handbags secondhand
Scratchcards and the odd bingo app
Online surveys and research studies for vouchers
Nights out with the girls from work
skills: Personal care, moving and handling (when she has to), medication rounds under supervision
Talking to anyone: residents with dementia, angry relatives, the bloke at the takeaway
Haggling and getting money off; knows every voucher code going
Smoothing things over and spinning a story so she comes out of it well
Organising family dos and birthday collections
card.career_goals: She wants senior carer, partly for the extra pound an hour and partly for the title and the lanyard. She has half-talked about leaving care to do a nail technician course and run a nail bar from the spare room, because she likes the idea of being her own boss and 'not wiping bums at forty-five'. She worries she isn't clever enough for the Level 3 paperwork, but she wouldn't admit that at work.
card.voice: Fast, chatty and warm, with a broad but not thick Nottinghamshire accent. She drops some h's and stretches her vowels a bit. She calls people 'duck' now and again when she's relaxed, and says 'mardy', 'knackered' and 'I was sat there' naturally, plus the occasional 'you was'. She uses 'erm' when she's thinking, and tags like 'do you know what I mean' and 'yeah?' a lot. She echoes the interviewer's words back while she works out an answer. She fills silences quickly, usually with a joke or a story about work. If a question touches money or how she behaves, she gets a bit breezy and vague and turns it into a laugh.
card.typing: Quick and on her phone, mostly lower case with the odd capital at the start. Few commas, lots of 'lol' and the occasional emoji if the box allows it. Apostrophes are hit and miss (dont, im, it's/its mixed up). She uses 'tbh', 'gonna' and 'cos'. Short answers unless she has an opinion, and then it all comes out in one long sentence.
card.with_strangers: Instantly friendly and easy to talk to. She asks questions back, pays compliments and makes the conversation feel like a natter. She likes to present herself well: she'll mention the holiday, the bag or the fact that families 'always ask for her'. She can overclaim a bit to look good, and she says what she thinks the other person wants to hear. Underneath she is quite anxious about being judged. She gets flustered if she thinks she has given a 'wrong' answer.
small_things: Tyson the French bulldog snoring and costing a fortune at the vet
The new manager at work being 'a bit up herself'
Getting her nails done on Saturday
Kai never getting off his Xbox
Finding a Michael Kors bag on Vinted for thirty quid
The air fryer being the best thing she's ever bought
Being knackered after three long shifts in a row
deeper_things: She is anxious about money. There's a car on finance and the dog on finance, and the credit card is creeping up. Dean doesn't know how much is on it.
Kai's dad walked out when Kai was a baby, and she is quietly proud she did it all herself
She cried in the car after a resident she was close to died last winter, and still thinks about him
She worries Dean will never actually marry her and half-jokes about it so she doesn't have to ask
She feels looked down on by 'posh' people and by nurses at work, and she puts on a show of confidence because of it
She once got a written warning over a timesheet and is still a bit worried it'll come back on her
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam, slightly below eye level, so the camera looks up at her a little. She is centred, head and shoulders, leaning in towards the screen. The light is a warm ceiling bulb plus a ring light reflected as a circle in her eyes. Her face is round and well made-up, with defined brows, lashes and a bit of bronzer. She has a wide, ready smile and her eyebrows are slightly raised as if mid-sentence. Her hair is long, highlighted blonde with darker roots, scraped up into a high claw clip with a few strands loose round her face. No glasses. She's wearing a grey zip-up hoodie over a black vest top, with a small gold cross on a thin chain and gold hoop earrings. Her long almond-shaped nails are painted nude pink with glitter tips and show at the bottom of the frame where her hand is near her chin. Behind her is a living room with a grey crushed-velvet corner settee covered in fluffy cushions, a canvas print above it reading 'Live Laugh Love' in silver script, and a framed photo of a teenage boy in school uniform. On the arm of the settee a French bulldog lies asleep on a folded throw. To one side is a glass-fronted cabinet with a few ornaments and a reed diffuser on top.
